title: Day 763: Sinaloa Congress Names Graciela Domínguez Nava Interim Governor, Vows to Prioritize Peace
detail: The Sinaloa Congress convened an extraordinary session on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 and voted 36-4 (PAN and PRI opposed) to name Graciela Domínguez Nava — Rubén Rocha Moya's former Secretary of Public Education and Culture, a federal deputy for Morena (2024-2027) and ex-PRD state deputy — as interim governor following Rocha Moya's indefinite second leave. She took oath at 9:00 AM and will serve through the term's end on October 31, 2027, becoming Sinaloa's second interim governor of 2026 after Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde (who held the post May 3–August 21). Domínguez immediately chaired her first State Cabinet meeting at the Salón Gobernadores of the Palacio de Gobierno in Culiacán, declaring 'nuestra prioridad será la paz' ('our priority will be peace') and pledging a comprehensive governance-and-security plan the following week, plus weekend touring of all three state regions and outreach to agricultural, fishing, tourism and business sectors. President Claudia Sheinbaum, who said she learned of the appointment during her own morning press conference, called Domínguez 'a honest woman with many years fighting for social justice' and clarified the choice was Congress's, not the presidency's, while pledging federal coordination on security.

media.caption: Graciela Domínguez Nava is sworn in as interim governor of Sinaloa, August 25, 2026

title: Day 763: SEDENA Airlifts 300 More Troops to Mazatlán as Sinaloa Reinforcement
detail: At 10:30 AM on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, SEDENA airlifted 300 Mexican Army personnel aboard two Air Force Boeing 737 heavy-transport aircraft from Santa Lucía Military Air Base (State of Mexico) to Mazatlán International Airport, incorporating them into 9th Military Zone operations under the National Public Security Strategy 2024-2030. SEDENA said the troops would conduct patrols, ground reconnaissance and deterrent actions in priority areas, aimed at dismantling criminal cells and detaining violence generators, in coordination with state and municipal authorities and 'con apego a la Ley Nacional sobre el Uso de la Fuerza' (in accordance with the National Law on the Use of Force) and human-rights standards.

media.caption: Mexican Army personnel arrive at Mazatlán International Airport as part of a 300-troop reinforcement, August 25, 2026
